title: Marine Net Gain: from theory to delivery
speaker: Jonathan Abbatt
abstract: Governments and industry are increasingly interested in Net Gain policies that aim to leave nature in better condition after development. Although these models are taking hold on land, transferring them to the sea is difficult. Offshore wind farms sit in complex ecosystems where changes spread over wide areas and are shaped by many human activities. Open questions include who governs marine spaces, how gains could be measured, and how Net Gain would fit alongside marine planning and conservation law. The talk examines whether land-based Net Gain approaches suit offshore settings, and whether a wider strategy for tackling cumulative marine pressures could produce more effective, lasting ecological improvements.

title: The development of high-integrity private investment in the restoration of nature in Scotland: opportunities and risks
speaker: Ross Johnston
abstract: Interest in how private investment can help address the nature and climate crises is growing worldwide. In 2022 the Scottish Government committed to creating a public-sector partnership to build a values-led, high-integrity market for responsible private investment in Scotland. The partnership's work is set out in the 2024 Natural Capital Market Framework, which covers both managing risks and developing opportunities. The talk reviews progress on this commitment to date and shares views on future actions.
